_doc: ENC-TSK-P15 / ENC-ISS-669. Pinned, hash-verified snapshot of NX-2021-L/devops's OWN declared Lambda estate -- built in reverse of the pattern devops already uses for the enceladus shared library (NX-2021-L/devops scripts/fetch_shared_library.py: a pinned immutable commit SHA plus a recorded sha256 per source module, where a stale digest is a hard build failure, never a warning). Enceladus CI cannot read a private sibling repo at check time without a token, so unlike fetch_shared_library.py this file cannot fetch devops over the network at build time -- it is a COMMITTED snapshot, refreshed by hand, by someone with read access to NX-2021-L/devops, whenever devops's Lambda estate changes. tools/verify_devops_ownership_snapshot.py checks this file's own internal consistency on every CI run (schema, no duplicate names, digest shape) and, when the DEVOPS_OWNERSHIP_LOCAL_SOURCE environment variable points at a local checkout of NX-2021-L/devops, re-hashes every declared source file and hard-fails on any mismatch -- the same digest-mismatch-is-a-refusal discipline fetch_shared_library.py enforces in the other direction. tools/verify_lambda_arch_parity.py's cross-source reconciliation (ENC-ISS-669 AC-6) reads functions[].function_name from this file as the complete set of names owned by NX-2021-L/devops: a live Lambda matching one of these names resolves to NOT_APPLICABLE_ON_PLANE, not a silent skip and not an unclassifiable failure. PREFERRED LONG-TERM SHAPE: devops publishes its own ownership artifact (mirroring how NX-2021-L/enceladus is fetched today -- publicly readable at a pinned commit) and enceladus fetches and verifies it at build time the same way fetch_shared_library.py does. That is not possible today because NX-2021-L/devops is a private repository and no token is wired into enceladus CI -- this snapshot is the interim, and the interim-ness is deliberate, not an oversight: see ownership_predicate below for why a name-prefix heuristic could not stand in for it.
pinned_by: ENC-TSK-P15, verified against a local read-access checkout of NX-2021-L/devops at the pinned commit (origin/main resolved to the same SHA at verification time)

infrastructure/analytics-stack.yaml.reason: devops's own top-of-tree deploy manifest. Its components.lambdas.manifest field points at infrastructure/aws/lambda/functions.yaml -- included here because that pointer is what makes functions.yaml the thing a naive predicate would stop at, and a change to this pointer (e.g. retargeting components.lambdas.manifest elsewhere) must invalidate this pin.

infrastructure/aws/lambda/functions.yaml.reason: devops's declared Lambda deploy manifest for the 'Deploy Analytics Stack' workflow. FOUR functions -- this is exactly the source a naive predicate would read and stop at, which is why ENC-ISS-669 found a fifth, live, devops-owned function invisible to enceladus: devops-io-devops-mcp appears nowhere in this file.

scripts/deploy_io_devops_mcp.py.reason: devops-io-devops-mcp's FUNCTION_NAME constant lives here, not in functions.yaml. The script's own docstring says why: 'Self-contained -- it does not import scripts/deploy_analytics_stack.py or drive off infrastructure/analytics-stack.yaml. This function's shape ... is specific to it and does not belong in the shared analytics-stack manifest.' That is a deliberate devops-side design choice enceladus has no standing to change -- it is exactly why the ownership predicate cannot be 'read functions.yaml' alone.

.github/workflows/deploy-io-devops.yml.reason: the workflow that actually invokes deploy_io_devops_mcp.py -- on push to services/lambda/devops_mcp/**, on a weekly JWKS re-bake schedule, and on workflow_dispatch. Corroborates that devops-io-devops-mcp is a live, actively-deployed function, not a dead script nobody runs.

ownership_predicate: Any Lambda function whose FunctionName exactly matches one of functions[].function_name in this file is owned by NX-2021-L/devops (owning_repo above) and is NOT_APPLICABLE_ON_PLANE to every enceladus deploy-validation and architecture-parity check, regardless of its resolved architecture or runtime. Membership is by exact name match against THIS FILE -- never a name-prefix heuristic. enceladus's own lambda_workflow_manifest.json independently declares dozens of its OWN functions that also carry a 'devops-' prefix (devops-changelog-api, devops-coordination-api, devops-graph-sync, ...), a historical naming holdover from before the two repos split -- a prefix-based predicate would misclassify enceladus's own functions as devops-owned (false exception) or, read the other way, would need to somehow exclude those, which just reproduces this file's job worse. See tools/verify_lambda_arch_parity.py's _validate_cross_source_reconciliation (ENC-TSK-P15 AC-6) for the read point, and infrastructure/lambda_workflow_manifest.json's architecture_exceptions.prod.permanent.families.devops_owned for the governance record (rationale, terminal_state, ratchet).
